segments.contextAfter: On iOS, an app is in use when it’s in the foreground and for a short time when it transitions from the foreground to the background. If the system terminates the app or the app isn’t running, the system doesn’t launch an app with When in Use authorization to deliver new updates; it does launch an app with Always authorization for some types of location updates.

```swift
func locationManagerDidChangeAuthorization(_ manager: CLLocationManager) { 
    switch manager.authorizationStatus {
    case .authorizedWhenInUse:  // Location services are available.
        enableLocationFeatures()
        break
        
    case .restricted, .denied:  // Location services currently unavailable.
        disableLocationFeatures()
        break
        
    case .notDetermined:        // Authorization not determined yet.
       manager.requestWhenInUseAuthorization()
        break
        
    default:
        break
    }
}

```
